data.one_liner: Minimal responsive framework using Bootstrap breakpoints by default with optional code generation.
data.what_it_does: Provides widgets and utilities like ResponsiveValue, ResponsiveChild, and ResponsiveParent to build screen-size-aware UIs. It supports Bootstrap breakpoints out of the box and allows custom breakpoints through code generation.
use_when: You want a minimal responsive framework based on Bootstrap breakpoints
You need to adapt widget properties, children, or wrapping widgets based on screen width
You want to define custom breakpoints using a JSON file and code generation
avoid_when: You need complex navigation-level adaptive layouts that aren't covered by basic width checks
You prefer heavy platform-adaptive widget libraries
strengths: Easy to use with straightforward widgets like ResponsiveValue and ResponsiveChild
Supports custom breakpoints via a screen_sizes.json file and code generation
Falls back to the nearest smaller defined screen size automatically
weaknesses: Relies on a custom code generation script (`dart run responsiveness`) rather than standard build_runner if using custom breakpoints
data.setup_notes: To use custom breakpoints, create a screen_sizes.json file at the root of the project and run `dart run responsiveness`.

alternatives.why_pick_it: More feature-rich framework for scaling and handling responsive layouts across different screen sizes.
